# NKE — Quantitative Attractiveness Report
**Decision date: 2026-05-08 | Instrument: NIKE, Inc. (NKE)**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin & Cash-Flow Trajectory

Nike's top line is essentially stalled. Q3 FY2026 (period ending 2026-02-28) delivered revenue of $11.28B, a mere +0.1% YoY versus $11.27B in Q3 FY2025, and a -9.2% sequential decline from Q2's $12.43B. Revenue has oscillated in a narrow $11.27B–$12.43B band over the last five quarters with no discernible growth trend.

The real deterioration is in profitability. Despite flat revenue, diluted EPS plunged to $0.35 in Q3, down -35.2% YoY from $0.54 and -34.0% QoQ from $0.53. Net income fell to $520M (from $794M YoY). Gross profit declined -3.1% YoY to $4.53B as cost of revenue rose from $6.59B to $6.75B. The operating income collapse is starker: $650M in Q3 versus $844M a year earlier (-23%), implying operating expenses climbed meaningfully even as the top line held flat. Operating margin has compressed to 5.8% (Q3), down from 7.5% a year ago. Net margin stands at 4.6%.

Cash generation has deteriorated in parallel. Operating cash flow in Q3 was $430M, down -76.0% YoY from $1.79B in Q3 FY2025 (which itself was seasonally strong). Even on a sequential basis, OCF fell -25.7% from Q2's $579M. The first three reported quarters of FY2026 show OCF of $430M, $579M, and $222M — all well below FY2025 comparative quarters.

## 2. Earnings Quality & Balance-Sheet Resilience

The earnings quality concern is severe. Revenue is flat, yet costs are rising, producing a margin squeeze that is accelerating. The gross margin at ~40.2% (Q3: $4.53B/$11.28B) remains above many consumer peers but is well below Nike's historical 44–46% range. Operating margins at 5.8% signal the company's cost structure has not reset to match its current revenue base.

On the balance sheet, total equity is $14.09B against total liabilities of $22.97B (latest quarter). The debt-to-equity ratio of 1.63x (total liabilities/equity) is elevated but not distressed. Total assets of $37.06B remain roughly stable quarter-to-quarter, suggesting no forced asset liquidation. However, rising liabilities and contracting earnings power erode retained earnings generation, which will pressure equity over time if trends persist.

The absence of free-cash-flow data makes a full cash-conversion assessment impossible. Operating cash flow of $430M against net income of $520M yields an OCF/NI ratio of 0.83x — acceptable, but the absolute dollar level is weak.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History

The current P/E (diluted) is 29.2x, which sits roughly mid-range of the 12-month window (19.1x–38.9x). However, this is deeply misleading as a standalone metric. The P/E is elevated *because earnings have collapsed*, not because the market is pricing growth. One year ago (2025-05-08), the stock traded at 19.3x with net margins of 9.4% and ROE of 32.2%. Today: 29.2x, net margin 4.8%, ROE 16.0%. The multiple has expanded by ~51% while the earnings power underneath has been cut in half.

P/B has compressed from 6.2x to 4.7x — the low end of its 4.5x–8.4x range — reflecting the price decline rather than genuine cheapness. Price-to-sales at 1.41x is unremarkable for a branded consumer company with contracting margins.

Earnings yield of 3.4% compares unfavorably to the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.41%, meaning NKE's earnings power is *below* the risk-free rate — an unusual and unfavorable condition for an equity.

## 4. Price Context Versus Fundamentals

NKE shares closed at $44.41 on 2026-05-07, near the 52-week low of $42.09 (high: $80.17). The quarterly decline is -29.2% (from $62.70 on 2026-02-05). The stock has fallen in three of the last four quarterly intervals: -18.9% (Aug–Nov 2025), +2.4% (Nov 2025–Feb 2026), and -29.2% (Feb–May 2026).

This price action is *directionally consistent* with the fundamental deterioration — the market is repricing a business whose earnings power is eroding. The price decline has not "overshot" fundamentals when measured against the trajectory of margins and cash flow. A 29x P/E on 4.6% net margins with declining OCF does not constitute a capitulation valuation.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

The macro backdrop adds a modest headwind. WTI crude oil at $98.38/bbl (+52.4% over the lookback window) raises input cost pressure for a consumer discretionary manufacturer — relevant to Nike's cost of goods sold and logistics. The 10-year Treasury yield at 4.41% makes the 3.4% earnings yield on NKE unappealing on a relative basis. The 10y-2y spread has narrowed to 0.49% from 0.74% three months prior, signaling flattening yield curves. VIX at 17.08 is elevated but off its late-March spike (31.05), indicating lingering but moderating risk sentiment.

News sentiment is deeply negative: mean score of -0.317 across 69 articles, with the last five scoring days all at -1.0 or -0.5. This is a mood thermometer confirming the fundamental narrative — deteriorating results and pessimistic outlook.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** If the operating cost structure is a temporary investment cycle (e.g., restructuring, DTC transition costs) and margins can revert toward the 8–10% operating range seen in prior years, the current earnings trough could prove temporary. At normalized EPS of ~$1.50–$2.00, the stock at $44 would represent 22–29x — still not cheap, but more defensible. P/B at 4.7x is at the floor of the historical range, providing some valuation support.

**Downside:** Revenue stagnation persists, operating expenses remain elevated, and margins compress further. A sub-4% operating margin is plausible if cost discipline fails and revenue erodes. At current trajectory, ROE (16%) and margins (4.8% net) are still compressing — there is no evidence of a trough forming. Cash generation is shrinking, limiting buyback capacity and signaling potential dividend risk.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

**Fundamentally unattractive at current levels.** NKE exhibits flat revenue, sharply declining margins and earnings, deteriorating cash generation, and no visible inflection. The 29x P/E is misleading — it reflects depressed earnings, not attractive entry pricing. Earnings yield (3.4%) sits below the risk-free rate (4.41%). The stock's -29% quarterly decline is explained by the fundamental trajectory, not by overshooting it. Until operating margins stabilize or revenue reaccelerates, the risk/reward skews negative. A bottom-fisher would need to see at least one quarter of margin stabilization or earnings re-acceleration before the quantitative case improves. There is no quantitative evidence of fundamental attractiveness as of the decision date.

## NKE — Qualitative Franchise & Risk Report
**Decision Date: 2026-05-08 | Evidence window: ~April 8 – May 7, 2026**

---

### 1. Business / Franchise Read

Nike remains the world's most valuable sportswear brand (brand value near $30B, per Statista 2026) and holds the largest single share of global athletic footwear — estimated at ~38% (matrixbcg.com, Apr 2026) though a separate Euromonitor-sourced analysis pegs the figure closer to 22.9% in 2025, down ~3pp YoY for the third consecutive year (logos-pres.md, ~May 2026). The discrepancy likely reflects market definition, but both sources agree the trend is erosion, not stability.

**Revenue model:** ~68% footwear, ~25% apparel, ~7% equipment/other (fourweekmba.com, Mar 2026). FY2025 total revenue was $46.3B, down from $51B+ in FY2023 and FY2024 — a meaningful structural decline, not a single-quarter miss (fourweekmba.com; Statista 2026). The Jordan Brand remains a franchise asset generating ~$6.6B in FY2023, and Converse contributes ~$2.4B.

**Distribution shift:** Under new CEO Elliott Hill (appointed late 2024), Nike pivoted from an aggressive direct-to-consumer strategy back toward wholesale partnerships with Foot Locker, Dick's, and JD Sports. DTC is now ~44% of revenue (matrixbcg.com, Apr 2026). Structural sources frame this as a correction of prior management's over-indexing on Nike Direct, which damaged retailer relationships and shelf presence.

**Competitive moat:** Nike's advantages remain brand equity, a $4B+ annual demand-creation budget, an elite athlete roster, and a patent portfolio exceeding 25,000 (matrixbcg.com competitive landscape, Apr 2026). However, niche performance brands — On Running (30%+ YoY revenue growth) and Hoka — are eroding running-category dominance, while Chinese domestic brands are gaining share in Greater China (matrixbcg.com; fool.com, May 6).

---

**Q3 FY2026 specifics (ended Feb 28, 2026):** Revenue $11.28B flat YoY reported, down 3% currency-neutral. Wholesale +5% reported; NIKE Direct −4% reported, −7% currency-neutral. EPS $0.35 vs. $0.54 prior year (businesswire). Consensus EPS for current FY is $1.51, implying a −30.1% YoY decline (finance.yahoo.com, ~May 2026).

---

### 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Risks:**
- **Margin compression:** Net profit margin collapsed from ~12.8% (2021) to 4.8% in Q3 FY2026. Operating margins below 6% with heavy discounting (~37% of assortment) leave little buffer.
- **China deterioration:** Sales fell 10% in the region; consumer preference shifting to domestic brands. Tariff retaliation adds headwinds. Adidas has recovered there; Nike has not yet.
- **Regulatory/ESG overhang:** EEOC DEI investigation (public since ~May 2026) adds legal cost, management distraction, and reputational risk during a critical turnaround period. Separately, supply-chain wage-theft allegations from Asian garment workers and Oregon tax-break criticism layer additional ESG pressure (simplywall.st, ~Apr-May 2026).
- **Dividend sustainability:** FCF coverage of the dividend is stretched; earnings down 35% YoY. The $0.41 quarterly dividend was affirmed (May 4), but structural sources question durability.
- **Innovation pipeline gap:** Per Morningstar (cited in logos-pres.md), problems remain "systemic" — from inventory management to product-line adaptation to performance-first demand trends.
- **Competition intensifying:** On and Hoka gaining share in performance running; Chinese brands gaining in Greater China; Lululemon in athleisure. Nike's share decline is third consecutive year (logos-pres.md).

**Offsets:**
- **Brand equity is real and durable:** $30B brand valuation, cultural resonance via Jordan (~$7B revenue), and unmatched marketing scale provide a foundation that niche competitors cannot replicate quickly.
- **Management reset is underway:** Hill's pivot back to wholesale, 14,000 cumulative layoffs, and renewed innovation focus (Vomero 18, Alphafly refresh, "Project Amplify" personalization) represent genuine strategic correction.
- **Scale and balance sheet:** $46B revenue base, investment-grade credit, and $18B share-repurchase authorization provide financial flexibility. Institutional owners (Vanguard ~8.5%, BlackRock ~7.2%) are engaged.
- **Wholesale recovery early signal:** Wholesale revenue grew 5% in Q3 FY2026, suggesting channel re-engagement is taking hold.
- **Valuation reset:** Stock at lowest since 2014; multiple compression may already price in substantial downside.

---

### 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Negative-leaning with conditional upside.**

Nike possesses an undeniably strong franchise — global #1 brand, Jordan ecosystem, scale, and cultural relevance. However, the current evidence paints a picture of a business in genuine structural distress, not merely a temporary earnings dip. Revenue is declining, margins have been gutted, market share is eroding for the third straight year, competition is accelerating on multiple fronts, and China — once a growth engine — is contracting. The EEOC investigation and ESG criticisms add non-trivial governance and reputational risk during a period that demands focused execution.

The new CEO's strategic corrections (wholesale rebuild, layoffs, innovation refocus) are directionally right, but the evidence shows early-stage and uneven progress — wholesale is recovering while DTC declines, and management itself has lowered the recovery timeline. The dividend affirmation signals confidence but may prove optimistic given FCF constraints.

For fundamental attractiveness: the franchise quality remains above average, but the turnaround execution risk is high, the timeline is extending, and margin recovery is now projected no earlier than Q2 2027. The stock's cheapness is justified by the risk profile; this is not yet a compelling risk-reward on the qualitative evidence alone.

views.rationale: NKE is a structurally deteriorating business with no visible fundamental inflection. Revenue is flat ($11.28B Q3 FY2026, +0.1% YoY) while profitability is collapsing: EPS down 35.2% YoY to $0.35, operating margin compressed to 5.8% (from 7.5%), net margin at 4.6% (from 9.4% a year ago). Operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. The 29.2x P/E is misleading — it reflects depressed earnings, not cheapness; earnings yield of 3.4% sits below the 4.41% risk-free rate. Market share is eroding for the third consecutive year (down ~3pp to 22.9% per Euromonitor). Management has lowered the recovery timeline, delaying gross margin expansion to Q2 2027 and guiding for low-single-digit revenue declines for three more quarters. Short interest has surged to 4.67% of float. The EEOC DEI investigation, 14,000 layoffs, and 37% of assortment sold at discount signal a business in genuine structural distress. The stock's -29.2% quarterly decline and -32% YTD are directionally consistent with fundamentals, not an overshoot. No near-term catalyst exists to re-rate the stock; the earliest margin recovery is Q2 2027. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, no valuation support (earnings yield below risk-free), and absence of a near-term re-rating catalyst — align negatively.
